runs.text:
Light is not a thing but a
way of seeing. The same room
holds a different room at
noon and at dusk, and the
walls keep both of them.

We name the hours by the sun
and then forget the sun, as
if the clock were a kind of
weather of its own, made of
metal and glass in the hall.

A window frames the same
street all day long. Only
the shadows move across it,
drawing slow lines on the
floor and then erasing them.

Ask ten people what light is
and you will hear ten
answers, none of them wrong:
a particle, a wave, a gift,
a habit of the morning.

The oldest lamp in the house
still sits above the door,
though nothing is lit with
it now. It keeps the shape
of the light it used to give.

Between the two columns of
this page runs a narrow
gutter, and the eye crosses
it without a sound, one
line after the other.
